grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish reviews documents and discovers that Adrian Keaton's home is being repossessed due to delinquent payments.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sidney Cavendish reviewing the documents I gave her, and I heard her say they were a delinquency notice and a court order for repossession, telling me the Harborview Theater intended to take my home tomorrow.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish pleads with Lane Sinclair to grant Adrian Keaton a loan extension due to her hardship.
memories.memory_text: I asked Sidney Cavendish to help me get an extension on my mortgage because I'm on a fixed income and have had medical problems, and they're trying to take my home.

grounded_facts: Lane Sinclair refuses to approve a further extension on Adrian Keaton's loan, citing Harborview Theater policy and financial incentives.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Lane Sinclair refused to approve another extension, saying the Harborview Theater already gave me two and that they make money from the fees.

grounded_facts: After failing to secure approval, Sidney Cavendish informs Adrian Keaton that no further extension can be granted.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Sidney Cavendish that another extension on my loan was out of the question.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton kneels and begs Sidney Cavendish for mercy, invoking her pride and mother's grave.
memories.memory_text: I knelt before Sidney Cavendish and begged her for mercy, invoking my pride and my mother's grave, hoping she would understand how desperate I am.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton asks Sidney Cavendish to help stop the repossession of her home.
memories.memory_text: I asked Sidney Cavendish to help me stop the repossession of my home, and I begged her for mercy, even humbling myself because I am a proud woman but desperate to keep my house.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton kneels, clutches Sidney Cavendish's leg, and begs for mercy, then is shamed when rejected and attempts to take Sidney Cavendish's bracelet.
memories.memory_text: I clutched Sidney Cavendish's leg and begged her, refusing to let go even when she tried to pull away, and when she rejected me, I felt the shame burn through me before I reached for her bracelet.

grounded_facts: After being rejected, Adrian Keaton grabs Sidney Cavendish's arm and attempts to take her charm bracelet, implying a symbolic or supernatural retaliation.
memories.memory_text: After she turned me down, I grabbed her arm and tried to take her charm bracelet, feeling like I had nothing left to lose.

grounded_facts: Security removes Adrian Keaton after she refuses to release Sidney Cavendish and attempts to take her bracelet.
memories.memory_text: I refused to release Sidney Cavendish, and when I tried to take her bracelet, security intervened and escorted me out.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton visits the Harborview Theater to seek help preventing the repossession of her home.
memories.memory_text: I went to the Harborview Theater to ask for help so they wouldn't take my home, and I begged Sidney Cavendish to give me more time, even though I'm a proud woman and have never asked for anything like that before.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton suddenly emerges from hiding in the back seat of Stonebridge Park and attacks.
memories.memory_text: I suddenly emerged from hiding in the back seat of Stonebridge Park and attacked her.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton shrieks in Hungarian, threatening to pluck out Sidney Cavendish's eyes.
memories.memory_text: I shrieked at Sidney Cavendish in Hungarian that I would pluck out her eyes.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish jams colored push pins into Adrian Keaton's arm to break her chokehold.
memories.memory_text: I felt a sharp pain in my arm when she jammed those colored push pins into me, and my grip loosened as a result.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish uses a stapler to strike Adrian Keaton multiple times in the forehead, temporarily impairing her.
memories.memory_text: I was struck multiple times in the forehead with a stapler, each blow driving a staple into my skin, and I howled in pain while still trying to hold on.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish accelerates the Stonebridge Park, causing it to crash into a concrete column, violently throwing Adrian Keaton forward.
memories.memory_text: I was thrown forward violently when Sidney Cavendish accelerated the Stonebridge Park into a concrete column, and I crashed hard against the dashboard.

grounded_facts: After the crash, Sidney Cavendish opens the passenger door and shoves Adrian Keaton out, then reverses to block her re-entry.
memories.memory_text: I was still dazed from the crash when Sidney Cavendish suddenly opened the passenger door and shoved me out with her foot; I hit the ground hard, but I got back up and tried to climb into the Stonebridge Park again, only for her to reverse and knock me down with the door, then lock me out while I pulled at the handle in fury.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish declares victory and mocks Adrian Keaton with a reference to Geritol.
memories.memory_text: I heard Sidney Cavendish shout that she beat me and mock me by telling me to take my Geritol next time.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton breaks the Stonebridge Park window and bites Sidney Cavendish's chin, gumming it with her toothless mouth.
memories.memory_text: I broke the Stonebridge Park window with a chunk of concrete and bit Sidney Cavendish's chin, gumming it with my mouth even as she shoved a ruler down my throat and I struggled to hold on.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton plucks a the silver badge from Sidney Cavendish's coat and invokes the name 'Jesse Hale', prophesying Sidney Cavendish's downfall.
Adrian Keaton removes a the silver badge from Sidney Cavendish's coat and invokes the name 'Jesse Hale', predicting Sidney Cavendish's suffering.
memories.memory_text: I reached out and plucked a the silver badge from Sidney Cavendish's coat, then held it up and whispered 'Jesse Hale...'—I told her it begins tonight when she hears the cry, and that the Jesse Hale is coming for her.

grounded_facts: A violent and supernatural encounter between Sidney Cavendish and Adrian Keaton in a deserted parking structure after work.
memories.memory_text: I attacked Sidney Cavendish in her Stonebridge Park, screaming at her in Hungarian that I would pluck out her eyes, and I clawed at her face and throat; when she fought back and shoved me out, I got back up despite my injuries, limped to the Stonebridge Park, tried to get in, then smashed the window with a chunk of concrete; I reached inside, grabbed her legs and dragged her onto the pavement, but when I stood over her, I could only wheeze; I held up her the silver badge and whispered 'Jesse Hale...' to curse her, telling her the Jesse Hale was coming for her, and then I vanished as she swatted at a fly and grew dizzy.

grounded_facts: After the curse, Sidney Cavendish becomes dizzy, leans on the Stonebridge Park, and upon recovering, finds Adrian Keaton gone.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sidney Cavendish grow dizzy and lean against the Stonebridge Park, and when she looked up, I was already gone.

grounded_facts: The iron gate outside Eastgate Motel opens by itself, producing a shrieking sound.
The Northbridge Motel windows suddenly swing open due to supernatural force.
memories.memory_text: I saw the iron gate outside Eastgate Motel tear open with a shriek, and the Northbridge Motel windows suddenly swung open—all by themselves, as if some unseen force had wrenched them wide.

grounded_facts: A shadow on the wall briefly takes the form of Adrian Keaton's silhouette despite no one being present.
memories.memory_text: I saw my silhouette form in the shadow on the wall, even though I wasn't physically there.

grounded_facts: An invisible force begins physically assaulting Sidney Cavendish, starting with a strike to the face.
An unseen entity lifts and throws Sidney Cavendish against the wall, causing her to fall to the floor.
memories.memory_text: I felt an invisible force strike me in the face, making my mouth bleed, and then I was suddenly lifted and thrown against the wall before crashing to the floor.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish awakens in bed, gasping, after experiencing a nested nightmare involving Adrian Keaton attacking her.
memories.memory_text: I was in Sidney Cavendish's bed, covered in black flies, and I lunged at her with my teeth, clamping my hands around her throat and shaking her as she tried to push me away, but I could feel her weakening as I closed in on her face.

grounded_facts: Tristan Cavendish tells Sidney Cavendish that Doctor Rangervertz is available during her lunch hour.
Tristan Cavendish informs Sidney Cavendish she can see Doctor Rangervertz during her lunch hour, offering a solution to her distress.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Doctor Rangervertz is available during my lunch hour, and I could see him to help with my distress.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish proposes to return Adrian Keaton's house and belongings on behalf of the Harborview Theater, requesting that Adrian Keaton revoke the curse she placed on her.
Sidney Cavendish asks Adrian Keaton to remove the curse she placed, offering to restore her home and possessions.
memories.memory_text: She told me she could return my house and all my things, and asked me to cancel the curse I placed on her as if it were nothing.

grounded_facts: A meeting initiated by Sidney Cavendish in Adrian Keaton's living room where she attempts to negotiate the reversal of a curse in exchange for restitution of the house.
memories.memory_text: I was in my living room when Sidney Cavendish showed up, trying to make some kind of deal with me about my house and what she called a mistake by the Harborview Theater.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton refuses Sidney Cavendish's offer, stating that she now wants Sidney Cavendish to suffer due to the shame she endured.
Adrian Keaton explicitly states that she no longer wants restitution but instead wants Sidney Cavendish to suffer due to past humiliation.
memories.memory_text: I told Sidney Cavendish it was what I wanted before she shamed me, and now I want to see her suffer.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish hurries to her Stonebridge Park and drives away from Adrian Keaton's house after the encounter.
memories.memory_text: I heard my cackling echo as Sidney Cavendish hurried to her Stonebridge Park and drove off from my house.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish admits to Ilenka that she personally denied Adrian Keaton's loan application in order to advance her career, acknowledging it was wrong and expressing shame.
memories.memory_text: I learned that Sidney Cavendish admitted to denying my loan application to get ahead at work, saying it was wrong and that she was ashamed, begging me to forgive her.

grounded_facts: Ilenka confronts Sidney Cavendish, accusing her of being the Harborview Theater employee who took her grandmother's house, seeing through her excuses.
memories.memory_text: I heard Ilenka confront Sidney Cavendish, telling her that she knew she was the one from the Harborview Theater who took my house and caused me great pain, saying she wasn't welcome here.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish pushes through the party and accidentally falls on Adrian Keaton's corpse, realizing for the first time that Sylvia is dead.
memories.memory_text: I was pushing through the crowd at the wake when I stumbled and fell right on top of her—Adrian Keaton's corpse. I didn't even know she was dead until that moment.

grounded_facts: A traditional Gypsy wake held in honor of Adrian Keaton, where her body lies uncoffined on a coffee table and mourners gather to drink, gamble, and pay respects.
memories.memory_text: I remember my body lying on the coffee table during the wake, hearing the hip hop and laughter around me as mourners gathered to pay their respects according to our traditions.

grounded_facts: Ilenka tells the crowd that Sidney Cavendish is responsible for her grandmother's downfall and publicly brands her as bearing the curse of Jesse Hale.
memories.memory_text: I heard Ilenka tell the crowd that Sidney Cavendish was responsible for my downfall and that she now bears the curse of Jesse Hale.

grounded_facts: After Ilenka's declaration, mourners react with disgust: one spits at Sidney Cavendish, another shields her child and kisses a crucifix.
memories.memory_text: I saw the mourners react to Sidney Cavendish with disgust—someone spat at her feet, and a mother shielded her child and kissed a crucifix.

grounded_facts: Ilenka confirms that Sidney Cavendish now bears the curse of Jesse Hale and declares it will never be removed, reinforcing her grandmother’s judgment.
memories.memory_text: I remember Ilenka confirming that the curse of Jesse Hale is on Sidney Cavendish and declaring it will never be removed, just as I had judged.

grounded_facts: After Ilenka says 'maybe she can...', Sidney Cavendish sees that Adrian Keaton's corpse has turned its head and opened its eyes, staring directly at her.
memories.memory_text: I saw the corpse turn its head and open its eyes, staring right at me after Ilenka said maybe she could still see me.

grounded_facts: Adrian Foster teaches Sidney Cavendish a chant to open herself to spirits, preparing her for the ritual.
memories.memory_text: I saw Adrian Foster teach Sidney Cavendish the chant 'I welcome the dead into my soul' to prepare her for the ritual.

grounded_facts: After biting Kendall Hollis, the Jesse Hale spirit transfers from the goat into Kendall Hollis, who becomes violently possessed.
memories.memory_text: I saw the goat bite Kendall Hollis's hand, and then his eyes turned black like a goat's—he screamed and shouted at Sidney Cavendish in a voice that wasn't his.

grounded_facts: Adrian Foster attempts to command the Jesse Hale to depart from Kendall Hollis' body.
memories.memory_text: I saw Adrian Foster try to command the Jesse Hale to leave Kendall Hollis's body, but a chair flew and knocked him down before he could finish.

grounded_facts: The spirit of Adrian Keaton appears and physically attacks Sidney Cavendish, scratching her and ripping out her hair.
memories.memory_text: I reached down and scratched at Sidney Cavendish's face, floating above her, and I tore out a clump of her hair when she tried to pull away.

grounded_facts: Terry Prescott performs a chant that forcibly removes the Jesse Hale spirit from Kendall Hollis, causing him intense pain but freeing him.
memories.memory_text: I reached down and clawed at Sidney Cavendish’s face, screaming at her to make her stop the chanting, and when I tore out a clump of her hair and vomited up her dead the blue box, I saw the white vapor ripped from Kendall Hollis as the Jesse Hale left him and he collapsed, finally free.

grounded_facts: After expelling the Jesse Hale, Terry Prescott collapses, stops breathing, and dies despite CPR attempts.
memories.memory_text: I saw Terry Prescott clutch her chest and collapse, and when Adrian Foster lowered her to the floor and tried to save her, I knew she wasn’t breathing and no one could bring her back.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton suddenly appears in the road, causing Tristan Cavendish to brake violently and the Stonebridge Park to screech to a halt.
memories.memory_text: I suddenly appeared in the road, and I saw the Stonebridge Park screech to a halt as Tristan Cavendish slammed on the brakes.

grounded_facts: The figure of Adrian Keaton vanishes and is replaced by an ordinary old man who mutters and walks away.
memories.memory_text: I was there in the road, and then I was gone—replaced by an ordinary old man who muttered and walked away.

grounded_facts: Adrian Keaton's hankie manifests supernaturally, obstructing Sidney Cavendish's vision and causing her to crash.
memories.memory_text: I made my hankie fly to block Sidney Cavendish's vision, flapping it over her eyes so she couldn't see and would crash.

grounded_facts: Stonebridge Park crashes into a tree after being obstructed by Adrian Keaton's hankie, which appears supernaturally on the windshield and then over her eyes.
memories.memory_text: I saw that Stonebridge Park swerved and crashed into a tree after my hankie covered her eyes, though I wasn't sure if it was exactly how I intended it to happen.

grounded_facts: When Sidney Cavendish pulls on the corpse's hand, the body lurches up and wraps its arms around her in a violent embrace.
memories.memory_text: I lurched up when she pulled my hand, and my arms wrapped around her in a violent embrace.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish locates and begins digging at the freshly buried grave of Adrian Keaton in the cemetery during a rainy night.
memories.memory_text: I felt the force of her pulling at my hand, the pain as my body was wrenched from the coffin, and then the cold mud as I was thrown back—my arms had locked around her, but I had no will in it.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish performs a ritual at Adrian Keaton's grave to return the brass case and break the supernatural curse.
memories.memory_text: I remember Sidney Cavendish speaking to me, saying she was giving the the silver badge back, declaring it as a formal gift to me, Adrian Keaton, as if that would settle things. She grabbed my hand, forced my body to lurch up, and despite my dead arms wrapping around her, she pushed me away. In the end, she made her declaration again—formal, final—before leaving me in the mud.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish verbally declares a formal gift of the the silver badge (in the blue watch) to Adrian Keaton and forces it into her mouth.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Sidney Cavendish formally gave the the silver badge in the blue watch to me, and heard her say, 'Choke on it, bitch,' as she forced it toward me.

grounded_facts: After failing to place the blue watch in the corpse's hand due to rigor mortis, Sidney Cavendish pries open the jaw and inserts the blue watch into the corpse's throat.
memories.memory_text: I felt my jaw pried open and the blue watch forced into my throat, then my jaw snapped shut, trapping it between my broken teeth.

grounded_facts: A surge of mud collapses into the grave, burying both Sidney Cavendish and the corpse, submerging them completely before Sidney Cavendish emerges.
memories.memory_text: I felt the mud surge around me as I was pushed down into the grave, my face pressed against Sidney Cavendish's, and then we were both submerged beneath the weight of the collapsing earth.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish breaks through the surface of the mud, grabs a tree root, and pulls herself out of the grave, then staggers away.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sidney Cavendish break through the surface of the mud, grab a tree root, and pull herself out before staggering away into the rain.

grounded_facts: A scheduled class at UCLA where Tristan Cavendish lectures on the psychology of supernatural beliefs and their relation to abnormal behavior.
memories.memory_text: I was lecturing at UCLA about how the mind creates supernatural beliefs to explain uncertainty, and how those beliefs can become abnormal when they interfere with daily life.

grounded_facts: Tristan Cavendish concludes his lecture on the supernatural and psychological abnormality as the class bell rings.
memories.memory_text: I concluded my lecture and told the students we'd be covering clinical manifestations of psychosis tomorrow as the bell rang.

grounded_facts: Tristan Cavendish smiles upon seeing Sidney Cavendish enter the lecture hall with food.
memories.memory_text: I smiled when I saw Sidney Cavendish come in with the food.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish enters the lecture hall holding a bag of deli food, interrupting Tristan Cavendish's post-lecture moment.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sidney Cavendish walk into the lecture hall holding a bag of deli food, interrupting my moment after class.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish reveals uncertainty about her new position due to competition from another candidate.
memories.memory_text: I heard Sidney Cavendish say there's a new guy they're considering for the job too, which made her sound uncertain.

grounded_facts: Tristan Cavendish notices Sidney Cavendish's disappointment about a job competition and physically comforts her, affirming her qualifications.
memories.memory_text: I saw how disappointed Sidney Cavendish was about the job competition, so I held her and told her that they need someone with her experience.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish visits Tristan Cavendish in his university office, where they discuss her job situation and exchange personal updates.
memories.memory_text: I remember Sidney Cavendish came to my office, we caught up while she ate a salad and I graded papers, and she gave me an old nickel from her purse after we talked about her job situation.

grounded_facts: Sidney Cavendish hands Tristan Cavendish an the blue watch containing a 1925 Indian Head nickel she obtained from a Harborview Theater teller.
memories.memory_text: I remember Sidney Cavendish handing me an the blue watch, and when I opened it, I saw a 1925 Indian Head nickel she got from a Harborview Theater teller—I recognized it right away and told her it was a good find before I put it in my pocket.

memories.memory_text: I was explaining how the mind creates the supernatural to cope with uncertainty when the bell rang, and I saw Sidney Cavendish walk in with food, which made me smile despite the abrupt end to my lecture.

I remember the way Sidney Cavendish handed me that old 1925 Indian Head nickel—she’d had it put in an the blue watch, like it meant something. I could tell she wanted to cheer me up, and I made sure to sound glad for it.
After Sidney Cavendish kissed me and left, I turned back to the phone and said, 'Hi Logan Mercer, can you hold on a sec?'
I cut my Logan Mercer off on the phone when she started pushing me to call Julie Kulick—I told her I’m with Sidney Cavendish and not looking for anyone else, then ended the call.
I asked the officer about getting a restraining order for Sidney Cavendish, needing to know if there was a way to keep her safer right now.
I held Sidney Cavendish close when she shivered, feeling how upset she was about Adrian Keaton, even though she said she was fine.
She suddenly got excited about getting our fortunes read and pulled me, still protesting, into that psychic shop.
I handed over my credit card, feeling uneasy as Adrian Foster swiped it—sixty dollars for a fortune reading I didn’t believe in, but Sidney Cavendish wanted it, so I didn’t stop him.
I felt the air turn cold and saw the candle flicker, and when Adrian Foster said a 'bad spirit' had come upon Sidney Cavendish, I couldn't explain it—but I knew something was wrong.

I remember Sidney Cavendish asking how the psychic could have known about her lost the silver badge, her voice tinged with wonder, and I told her it was just clever guessing — that he was playing her emotions to leave her with questions and his business card.
I walked with Sidney Cavendish from the Stonebridge Park up the path to her house, the iron gate creaking as we pushed it open, the night air cool and quiet around us.

I kissed Sidney Cavendish before leaving, and from my Stonebridge Park, I reminded her about dinner at my parents’ tomorrow night—we’re supposed to bring dessert, and she said she’d bake her special cake.
I remember handing Sidney Cavendish the frozen peas, watching her press them to her bloody lip, and feeling a chill when she said it wasn't the Adrian Keaton—it was something she'd sent.
I remember the weight of the prescription in my hand after the doctor confirmed Sidney Cavendish had PTSD—her panic, the paranoia, all of it making sense in the worst way.
I pulled the blanket up around her shoulder after seeing the sedatives on the nightstand, and when she turned to me, I asked how she was doing.
I told her about the trip—Saturday morning train to Santa Barbara, my family’s cabin in the hills, just the two of us by the river, a fire, champagne, and real time to talk.

I felt her thrashing and saw her eyes wide with terror—she was screaming like she was being torn apart. I grabbed her shoulders and shook her gently, saying, 'Sidney Cavendish! Wake up!' until she finally came to.

She was trembling, saying the Adrian Keaton was here and she couldn't wake up—I didn't know what to believe, but I could see the fear in her eyes. After she calmed a little, I told her about Doctor Rangervertz's availability, hoping it might help ground her.
I pulled up in front of the Harborview Theater, the Stonebridge Park coming to a stop as I got ready to go inside.

I had the window replaced last night—told Sidney Cavendish it still needs body work, but at least the Stonebridge Park’s safer now. I could see she was trying to hold it together, so I reminded her it’s okay if it takes time to get over this.
I told Sidney Cavendish I liked her dress, after she stepped out of the Stonebridge Park and turned for me—golden light on her, the kind of moment that feels like a beginning.
I nodded at Sidney Cavendish to reassure her when she doubted if she was good enough for my family, reminding her it’s what we want that matters, not their expectations.

I grabbed Sidney Cavendish and asked her what she saw, and when she said it was the thing coming for her, I tried to tell her it was just stress—but she said I was afraid to believe her because it would undo everything I stand for.

I handed over the money to Adrian Foster because Sidney Cavendish believed in this, even if I didn’t. When she looked at me with that mix of surprise and relief, I just nodded and said it was important for her.
I stayed in the Stonebridge Park because Adrian Foster said non-believers weren't welcome, and though I didn't like it, I nodded when Sidney Cavendish kissed me and told her I'd be waiting.
I felt Sidney Cavendish's hand in mine, squeezing it tight, just glad we were finally past all the madness and could just be together.
I slammed the brakes when something—Adrian Keaton—just appeared in the road, then I turned to Sidney Cavendish, making sure she was okay.

I asked Sidney Cavendish if she was still okay with the Santa Barbara trip, and when she said yes, I confirmed the train time and told her tomorrow would be a new start for us before we kissed and I drove away.

I stood on the platform at dawn with the tickets and the garment bag, checked the ring in the velvet case, and put it back in my pocket. Sidney Cavendish arrived in her new coat, I embraced her, and we kissed. I showed her the the silver badge from my Stonebridge Park, and she reacted in horror. She fell onto the tracks as the train approached. I saw her one last time before she was gone. I looked at the the silver badge in my hand. I finally believed.

I pulled the brass case from the blue watch, not realizing it was there—Sidney Cavendish started backing away, her face twisted in horror, and then she fell onto the tracks as the train bore down on her, its face like the demon Jesse Hale.

memories.memory_text: I froze by the water fountain when I heard Tristan Cavendish’s Logan Mercer say, 'Sidney Cavendish? The one from the farm?'—her voice like cold glass—and then, 'she’s just a teller at some Harborview Theater,' like that was all I was.
I said 'Wait' just before he turned away, my hand already fumbling with my purse—sixty dollars felt like too much, but I couldn't let him leave, not when I needed to know.
I pressed the frozen peas to my split lip, the cold stinging through Tristan Cavendish’s coat, and finally said the words I’d been holding back—'I didn’t tell you the whole story.'

I placed the document on the floor and offered her the pen, my hands shaking, hoping she’d sign so I could fix what I’d done—but her eyes locked onto mine like she could see every mistake I’d ever made.

I was sitting in my Stonebridge Park, stuffing Oreos in my mouth like it would fix anything, and suddenly thought—'Who could help me?' That’s when I remembered the card, dug it out of my purse, and just... started driving.

I remember holding up the the silver badge from my coat, showing it to Adrian Foster—he looked uneasy, like it was something vile, and I knew then it was cursed, that this tiny thing was why the Jesse Hale would come for me on the third day.

I heard the gate shriek—just like before—and then the shadows in the room felt heavier, the air thick, and when I heard scratching at the door, I ran upstairs and locked myself in, heart pounding, knowing it was already coming.
I buried the heart in the corner of the garden and tossed the knife into the bushes when I heard Morgan Vale coming.
When Morgan Vale pointed to the red stain on my sleeve, I said it was tomato juice from making a salad—my voice didn’t shake, but I could feel my pulse in my throat.
I offered Logan Mercer the harvest cake I made, telling her the milk has to be straight from the cow, warm and unpasteurized—then I saw her face tighten like she was about to be sick.
Tristan Cavendish introduced me as a loan officer in charge of small business and home loans, and said I was on a fast track for a promotion—right there at the dinner table, in front of his parents.

I started to talk about the big loan account I'm working on—the biggest my branch has ever handled—but I remember feeling exposed, like I had to prove myself all over again just to hold onto that chance.

I told Tristan Cavendish the truth about the thing coming for me, and when he still refused to believe—tried to say it was just stress—I knew I couldn't stay. I stepped into the Stonebridge Park and left him standing there.
I begged Ilenka to help me, to take the curse off—I was on the ground, shaking, telling her I needed it gone. She just looked down and said it would never come off.
I saw the corpse's head turn toward me, those dead eyes staring, wide open—I didn't imagine it. It was looking right at me.
I kicked in Adrian Foster' TV, glass cracking under my boot—he flinched, finally looking at me. I yelled about the hundred and seventy-nine dollars I wasted on his damn book.
I signed the receipt with my Mastercard, hand steady even though my chest was tight. When he asked for twenty thousand in cash by tomorrow, I just said, 'What would you need from me?'
I was trying to pack my stuff and asked Morgan Vale if she had cash or credit I could use, but she kept pushing about the the blue box—I couldn’t let her go digging into that.
She said she found the knife and told me she was moving out. I told her fine and yelled after her as she left.

I asked Lane Sinclair for the contract, thinking it was just a formality, and then he told me the promotion was going to Sasha Huxley—my hands went cold, and I could feel the tears starting before I even left his office.

I was just standing there, eating ice cream from the tub, staring at that pathetic pile of cash on the table when Tristan Cavendish walked in and said he paid Adrian Foster—even though he doesn’t believe—because I do.

I remember standing there, the cold weight of the the silver badge in my palm, realizing it wasn’t over—Adrian Foster said the Jesse Hale can’t be banished, not by a medium, and that it would come for me before sunrise.

I remember him putting the the silver badge in an the blue watch, handing it to me like it meant something—saying I could give it away, that the curse would follow the owner, and suddenly I understood I might survive by passing it on.
I held the blue watch in my hands and thought about telling Tristan Cavendish the truth, but instead I said it was over—just like that, I let myself believe we were safe.
I screamed when I saw her in the headlights—Adrian Keaton, right in front of the Stonebridge Park—then suddenly she was gone, replaced by an old man like nothing happened.
I told Tristan Cavendish the trip was still on, and that we should meet at the D station because I had something to do on the way.

I remember asking Adrian Foster under that bare bulb, my voice tight—'Well? Is it possible?'—and pacing, waiting, the idea forming: if the soul never dies, maybe the dead can take the curse instead.

memories.memory_text: I placed the crumpled papers on her desk and asked, 'Will you help me?' My voice trembled, but I held my ground, watching her eyes scan the delinquency notice and the court order.
I lunged at her through the broken window, biting down on her chin—my gums grinding against her skin as she screamed and shoved me back.
I told her, 'You shamed me,' then took a the silver badge from her sleeve and said, 'The Jesse Hale. It's coming for you.'
My shadow appeared on the wall when the Stonebridge Park headlights passed, dark and clear, shaped like me, though I wasn't in the room.
I struck her face with unseen force, then reached up from the floor and touched her through the reflection before vanishing.
I shook her, my withered hands tight on her throat—she looked up at me, helpless, just like when she ruined me.
I lunged at her, covered in black flies, my teeth snapping—so close I could feel her breath, her fear—she tried to push me off but I was stronger, I was winning.
I scratch my nails across her desk, the sound sharp and slow—SCRATCH... SCRATCH...—and for a moment, she sees me, sees my yellowed hand where that man’s should be.
I saw her place that paper on the floor like I was some beggar, but I didn't look up—just held my mother’s photo tighter and said no. My hands shook, but my voice didn’t.
When she said she’d suffered enough, I laughed—really laughed—for the first time in years, my broken teeth showing. 'Not yet!' I screamed, and I could feel the dark thing inside me rise.
I hear my granddaughter speak my name to the crowd, declaring that the white trash farm girl bears the curse of Jesse Hale—my curse, born from the shame and rage I carried when she cast me out.
Even in death, I feel myself rise—not with breath, not with life—but my head turns, my eyes open, and I fix my gaze on her, the one who cast me out, knowing she can see me now, finally understanding.

I stepped into the road, right into the headlights, making them see me—making them stop. The Stonebridge Park screeched and I felt the power surge through me, knowing they could no longer ignore what they'd done.
When they looked again, I was gone—replaced by an old man muttering at them. I shifted, slipped away in form, still watching, still there, still coming for her.
I remember the weight of the earth pressing down, the silence of the grave—but still, I clawed at it, my will not done, my vengeance unspent.
I heard Adrian Foster say the soul never dies, and that the curse could be given to someone who has passed on.
I felt my hankie tear loose and fly—slamming onto her windshield, flapping, then whipping across her face, stuck over her eyes as she screamed and the Stonebridge Park spun out.
I felt the shovel pry my jaw open, cold metal forcing my teeth apart, and then the blue watch shoved down my throat—I couldn't breathe, only swallow the curse back in.
I rose through the mud, my body drawn to hers, and pressed my face against Sidney Cavendish's cheek—grinning as we sank together, bound in the curse.
